name: The Pastels
label: Creation Records
lede: Stephen McRobbie started the Pastels in Glasgow in 1981, cut three of Creation's first singles, and never moved the band out of Glasgow.

eras.title: Glasgow, after Postcard
eras.text: Postcard Records had shown Glasgow could make its own pop. Brian Taylor pulled together a band around Stephen McRobbie, who would become Stephen Pastel, and they started putting out singles on whichever small label would have them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Stephen McRobbie · Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Brian Taylor recruits Stephen McRobbie and the Pastels begin
years.p: [[Brian Taylor|8733c86a-bfd9-4b79-abda-93b5b978fe30]], later known as Brian Superstar, brings [[Stephen McRobbie|8b1a3394-d670-451c-9f41-94339f75042c]] in on guitar and vocals in Glasgow.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Wikipedia: Stephen McRobbie
years.h: 'Songs for Children' comes out on Whaam!
years.p: The debut single is Whaam! catalogue number 5, followed the same year by a cassette, Entertaining Edward. [[Martin Hayward|64808527-0c24-4c93-b53c-34ab8ed49e12]] joins on bass.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Rough Trade puts out 'I Wonder Why'
years.p: Single RT 137, backed with 'Supposed to Understand'. [[Bernice Simpson|fae3953c-dc87-4a9f-943b-6d3391385731]] takes over the drums the same year.

eras.title: Creation's fifth record
eras.text: Alan McGee's brand-new Creation Records needed bands, and the Pastels were on it from the start: three singles in under two years, all inside the label's first two dozen releases. Then they moved on.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Wikipedia: Up for a Bit
years.h: 'Something Going On' is Creation CRE 005
years.p: Backed with 'Stay With Me Until Morning Comes'. Annabel Wright, known as Aggi, joins on vocals and keyboards. She'll draw Pastels sleeves into the 2010s.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Getintothis
years.h: 'Million Tears' is CRE 011, one ahead of the Mary Chain
years.p: The Pastels' second Creation single sits right before CRE 012, [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]'s 'Upside Down'.

years.cap: Ad for the Pastels, Jowe Head and the Shop Assistants at Thames Poly
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Twee.net · Getintothis · Sheepish
years.h: 'I'm Alright With You' is the last Pastels single on Creation
years.p: CRE 023. The same year McRobbie starts his own Glasgow label, [[53rd & 3rd|81bcc253-1c8e-4384-a4d1-48b4e958c914]], with Sandy McLean and [[David Keegan|7c444986-69ab-47d0-942c-a3a42af213e7]].
years.xp: Its first release is the Shop Assistants' 'Safety Net'. [[BMX Bandits|3a369807-6de5-42ea-bbaa-37524ad6989c]] and Talulah Gosh follow, and [[The Vaselines|a70b63fd-cae7-4a5f-b338-b18343f3ee2f]] put out 'Son of a Gun' and 'Dying for It' on it in 1987 and 1988.

eras.title: A cassette in the NME, an album at last
eras.text: A track on the NME's C86 tape put the Pastels in the middle of a scene the press had just named. The first album took until 1987, made in a Leamington Spa studio, and the second took three sessions over two years.

years.src: Wikipedia: C86 · Wikipedia: The Pastels · Getintothis · The Line of Best Fit
yt: Live at the ICA, C86 week, July 1986
years.h: 'Breaking Lines' goes on the NME's C86 cassette
years.p: Side one, track ten, on the tape that opens with [[Primal Scream|55704c38-224f-4b75-b29f-d43653f8bc9a]]'s 'Velocity Girl'. The NME and the ICA put on a week of C86 gigs in London that July.
years.xp:
The song was a Pastels single on Glass that year, the flip of 'Truck Train Tractor'. 'Crawl Babies' followed, also on Glass.

The tag stuck harder than the band liked: in 2013 McRobbie told The Line of Best Fit they'd never felt it described them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Up for a Bit · Wikipedia: The Pastels · Getintothis
years.h: Up for a Bit with The Pastels arrives on Glass
years.p: Ten songs recorded in September 1986 at W.S.R.S. in Leamington Spa with producer John A. Rivers. Aggi draws the sleeve.
years.xp:
Kurt Cobain of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] was among its fans. The Guardian later credited it with giving Glasgow bands the confidence to stay home instead of moving south, a line that runs to [[Belle and Sebastian|e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70]] and [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]].

Getintothis called it "a classic pop record," with "an extra woolly jumper to keep the cold out." The Scotsman put it 37th on its list of the 100 best Scottish albums.
play: Up for a Bit with The Pastels

years.src: Wikipedia: Sittin' Pretty · Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Three sessions in Edinburgh make Sittin' Pretty
years.p: Recorded at REL between November 1987 and January 1989 with Richard Mazda, out on Chapter 22 in Britain and Homestead in the US. Hayward, Simpson and [[Eugene Kelly|d1779852-7f21-4658-b1fe-fc300faf5a61]] of [[The Vaselines|a70b63fd-cae7-4a5f-b338-b18343f3ee2f]] all leave after it.
years.xp: Trouser Press said the band sounded like it was "consciously trying to sound like themselves" for the first time. The Glasgow Herald heard Iggy Pop, Jonathan Richman and the Velvet Underground in it.

eras.title: Stephen, Aggi and Katrina
eras.text: A longtime fan on drums turned the Pastels into a trio, and the trio found friends all over: K Records in Olympia, Jad Fair, Domino in London, and a rotating crew of Teenage Fanclub guitarists.

years.src: Sheepish · Getintothis · Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Katrina Mitchell, a longtime fan, takes over the drums
years.p: [[Katrina Mitchell|b2849adb-f96a-44bc-985a-560acb9fa5e4]], who had played in Melody Dog, joins McRobbie and Aggi. The same year [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s K Records issues their 'Different Drum' single.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Wikipedia: Up for a Bit
years.h: A Daniel Johnston cover and a record with Jad Fair
years.p: 'Speeding Motorcycle', the [[Daniel Johnston|8a7ca8b0-d23c-4eff-8fe9-6220ba5c9c76]] song, comes out on Paperhouse, which also reissues the first album. The This Could Be the Night EP with [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] follows.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Brian Taylor leaves; David Keegan comes in on guitar
years.p: The band's co-founder steps away after eleven years. [[David Keegan|7c444986-69ab-47d0-942c-a3a42af213e7]] plays guitar through 2000.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Domino
years.h: Mobile Safari is the Pastels' first album on Domino
years.p: The Domino run started with the 1994 singles 'Olympic World of Pastelism' and 'Yoga'. Domino's own bio calls the record "Glaswegian West End classicism."

years.src: Wikipedia: Illumination · Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Illumination slows everything down
years.p: Recorded at Cava in Glasgow, with [[Gerard Love|05e9b21b-da4e-4dbf-8362-4ceedd501f80]] and [[Norman Blake|c9605929-6b48-4991-bb96-0bf460df8ee1]] of [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]] and [[Dean Wareham|a21a3ff2-064c-452d-8aea-3d4039ab70d6]] on guitars. AllMusic heard "subdued, lovely melodies."
years.xp: 'Unfair Kind of Fame' and 'The Hits Hurt' came out as singles that summer. A remix album, Illuminati, followed in 1998.

eras.title: Soundtracks, a shop, a label
eras.text: With Aggi gone to illustration, McRobbie and Mitchell became the Pastels' core. They scored a film, started the Geographic label through Domino, became partners in Glasgow's Monorail Music shop, and found an unlikely audience in Japan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Illumination · Wikipedia: The Pastels · The Quietus · The Skinny
years.h: Aggi leaves to work as an illustrator
years.p: Annabel Wright, on bass and vocals since 1990, steps away after 16 years; David Keegan leaves the same year. She keeps drawing for the band.
years.xp:
She had already decided against touring after Illumination, to put her time into painting. Her painting is the cover of Slow Summits thirteen years later.

McRobbie told The Skinny: "We probably would have made a record around 1999/2000 if Annabel hadn't left."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Last Great Wilderness
years.h: Jarvis Cocker sings on the Pastels' film soundtrack
years.p: The Last Great Wilderness comes out on Geographic. [[Jarvis Cocker|38550441-d437-4aff-867e-e79bf0c04142]] takes the lead on 'I Picked a Flower', with Richard Hawley and Bill Wells among the players.

years.cap: Stephen Pastel at All Tomorrow's Parties, Minehead, December 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels
years.h: Two Sunsets, made with Tenniscoats
years.p: A full album with the Japanese duo Tenniscoats, on Geographic.

eras.title: Sixteen years to the summit
eras.text: The next proper album took sixteen years, a few studios and a producer from Chicago. After it came collaborations, a record with Sonic Youth and music for the stage.

years.cap: Stephen Pastel at the Slow Summits launch, CCA, Glasgow, June 1, 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Slow Summits · The Skinny · DIY · The Line of Best Fit · The Quietus
years.h: Slow Summits ends a 16-year wait
years.p: Recorded in Glasgow and Chicago from 2010 to 2012 and co-produced by [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]]. Aggi Wright designed the cover; some songs went back to 1999.
years.xp:
Gerard Love and Norman Blake played on it again, with Ronald Lippok of To Rococo Rot and members of Tenniscoats. The Chicago sessions were at McEntire's Soma studio, booked on the rule that "whatever we did, that would be it."

They came out with about an hour of music. "We had to make some tough decisions as to what we'd leave out," McRobbie told DIY; a couple of the cut songs were as good as anything on the record. On the gap since Illumination: "It doesn't seem like that long, being in the middle of it all."

Drowned in Sound gave it 8/10 and called it "their most lovelorn" set yet. The touring band by then had Love, John Hogarty, Tom Crossley on flute and Alison Mitchell on trumpet.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pastels · Wikipedia: Stephen McRobbie
years.h: Sonic Youth and the Pastels Play the New York Dolls
years.p: A joint record with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], released on Glass Modern.

years.src: Domino · God Is in the TV
years.h: Stephen Pastel scores This Is Memorial Device for the stage
years.p: With Gavin Thomson, out on Geographic, for the Fringe First-winning stage version of David Keenan's 2017 novel about a made-up Airdrie post-punk scene.
years.xp:
Director Graham Eatough first asked for the music for a show at the Edinburgh International Book Festival; the Royal Lyceum helped develop it. Katrina Mitchell, John Hogarty and Tom Crossley play on the record.

"We wanted to be respectful. The novel's a total cult thing," McRobbie told God Is in the TV. He calls the album "a love letter".
